evidence: Full gakṣa gives Nepali/Bengali gāch, Assamese gās, Oriya gacha and Maithili gachiā tree. These support selected eastern affricate/sibilant tree forms and ordinary vowel endings. Source aspiration, nasalization and vowels remain intact; exact local developments and cross-IA transmission remain qualified. The grove senses of some gāchī comparanda do not change the survey tree gloss.

Full jhāṭa subsection 1 explicitly gives Gujarati jhāṛ tree/plant, Marathi jhāḍ tree and Hindi chāṛ bush alongside regional sibilant forms. These support the selected simple western jhaḍ/saḍ/chāḍ tree forms. Source affrication, sibilants, aspiration, retroflexion and final inflection remain intact; local phonetic history and cross-IA transmission remain qualified. No new Munda donor is asserted from Turner’s ultimate-origin suggestion.

Full būṭa subsection 2 būṭṭa explicitly lists Lahnda/Punjabi būṭā and West Pahari buṭṭ/būṭā tree, plus Kotgarhi bvṭṭi plant/tree. This supports selected northern u-vowel tree responses and their ordinary inflection. Source dental/retroflex notation, nasalization and vowels remain intact; local transmission is qualified. Distinct o-vowel and aspirated-head branches are not automatically conflated.

Full būṭa subsection 3 bōṭṭa explicitly gives West Pahari boṭṭ and Kumaoni/Nepali boṭ tree/stem/trunk. The selected Danuwar and Kului boṭ/botːe/botːiː tree forms match this o-vowel branch. Source gemination, vowels and inflection remain intact, with local development and cross-IA transmission qualified.
